subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept the bounded longer isolated-cron setup watchdog in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 as the fix for this issue, or require a lower cap or operator-tunable config surface first?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but changing the default setup wait from a fixed 60 seconds to a longer bounded window affects cron capacity and stuck-run availability behavior, which is a maintainer policy choice rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept bounded watchdog
options.body: Merge the open bounded-watchdog PR and own the longer stuck-setup occupancy as the preferred compatibility-free fix.

options.title: Tighten before merge
options.body: Ask for a lower cap or additional runtime proof if cron-slot occupancy under truly stuck setup is the main concern.

options.title: Require configurability
options.body: Pause the bounded default and require an explicitly approved config surface for operators with slow startup environments.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge the open bounded-watchdog PR and own the longer stuck-setup occupancy as the preferred compatibility-free fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the current cron watchdog owner boundary and the repo's high bar for new config/default behavior, and this history ties steipete to the relevant cron service refactor path.
